content.statement: Observables are Hermitian operators; outcomes are eigenvalues; probability P(aₙ) = |⟨aₙ|ψ⟩|²; state collapses to |aₙ⟩.
content.explanation: This is the standard projective measurement postulate.
content.example: For Z, outcomes ±1; |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩+β|1⟩ gives P(+1)=|α|², P(−1)=|β|².
keyTakeaways: Observables are Hermitian operators; outcomes are eigenvalues; probability P(aₙ) = |⟨aₙ|ψ⟩|²; state collapses to |aₙ⟩.
Know what problem or physical phenomenon 9.1 Measurement Postulate addresses.
Be able to interpret every symbol and state the assumptions behind the formula.

steps.text: Write |ψ⟩ = Σ_i c_i|i⟩ in the orthonormal eigenbasis of the observable.

steps.title: Project onto outcome i

steps.title: Apply Born rule
steps.text: Squaring the modulus gives the probability of observing outcome i.

codeExamples.code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.quantum_info import Statevector
import json

LESSON_ID = '09-9-1-measurement-postulate'
circuit = QuantumCircuit(1)
circuit.h(0)
from qiskit.primitives import StatevectorSampler
circuit.measure_all()
result = StatevectorSampler(seed=7).run([circuit], shots=512).result()
print(json.dumps({'lesson': LESSON_ID, 'counts': result[0].data.meas.get_counts()}))

content.statement: Positive Operator‑Valued Measure: a set {Eᵢ} with Eᵢ ≥ 0, ∑Eᵢ = I. Probability P(i) = Tr(ρEᵢ).
content.explanation: More general than projective measurements; can distinguish non‑orthogonal states imperfectly.
content.example: Unambiguous state discrimination of |0⟩ and |+⟩ uses POVM elements E₀ ∝ |−⟩⟨−|, E₁ ∝ |1⟩⟨1|, E? = I − E₀ − E₁.
keyTakeaways: Positive Operator‑Valued Measure: a set {Eᵢ} with Eᵢ ≥ 0, ∑Eᵢ = I.
Know what problem or physical phenomenon 9.6 POVMs addresses.
Be able to interpret every symbol and state the assumptions behind the formula.

content.statement: Unknown quantum states cannot be perfectly cloned.
content.explanation: Assume U exists such that U|ψ⟩|0⟩ = |ψ⟩|ψ⟩ for all |ψ⟩. For two states, ⟨ψ|φ⟩ = ⟨ψ|φ⟩², implying ⟨ψ|φ⟩=0 or 1, contradiction for arbitrary states.
keyTakeaways: Unknown quantum states cannot be perfectly cloned.
Know what problem or physical phenomenon 9.9 No‑Cloning Theorem addresses.
Be able to interpret every symbol and state the assumptions behind the formula.

formulas.description: Formula carried from the source curriculum; verify notation against the surrounding lesson.

steps.text: Let U act on |ψ⟩ and |φ⟩.
Then ⟨ψ|φ⟩ = ⟨ψ|φ⟩².
This only holds if the inner product is 0 or 1.

content.statement: Unknown quantum states cannot be deleted.
content.explanation: No unitary can map |ψ⟩|ψ⟩|A⟩ → |ψ⟩|0⟩|A′⟩ for arbitrary |ψ⟩. Quantum information is conserved.
content.example: Cannot erase a qubit without leaving a copy.
keyTakeaways: Unknown quantum states cannot be deleted.
Know what problem or physical phenomenon 9.10 No‑Deleting Theorem addresses.
